motive.canonical: Ruth is Marcus Bell's illegitimate half-sister, never acknowledged by the Bell family. Marcus was changing his will in a way that would have required Ruth to contest it publicly and protractedly. She killed him before the will was finalised so she could claim as next-of-kin on intestacy.

method.canonical: Poison — digitalis glycoside extracted from foxglove, added to Marcus's evening cocoa.

opportunity.canonical: Ruth had a spare key to Marcus's house and used it to enter at 21:00, adding the poison to the pre-prepared cocoa and burning a copy of the birth certificate in the study fireplace.

explanation: Correct. Ruth Calder killed Marcus Bell. Ruth is Marcus's illegitimate half-sister — Henry Bell's daughter by Doris Calder — never acknowledged by the Bell family despite living in the same village for twenty years. When Marcus revised his will to exclude Isabella and the clinic, he left a private note to his solicitor: 'if R. contests, she may have legal standing.' Ruth had confronted Marcus at 18:00 the previous evening; he told her to contest if she liked, but he would fight it. That night, Ruth harvested foxglove from her garden, extracted digitalis glycoside, and used her spare key to enter the house at 21:00. She added the extract to Marcus's pre-prepared cocoa and burned a copy of the birth certificate in the study. Marcus died in his chair at 22:40 of cardiac arrhythmia, indistinguishable from natural causes without targeted toxicology. The cracked vial in Ruth's fireplace ash, the cut foxgloves, the annotated pharmacy text, the mug residue, and — above all — the birth certificate hidden in the binding of a book in Marcus's study are the keys to this case.
